review.rationale: The supplied Gold is a coherent independent expectation for this pending-decision planning case. The original PRD, acceptance statements, stable REQ-001/AC-001 through AC-003/DEC-001 keys, repository identity and base commit agree with Gold. DEC-001 materially determines omitted-option behavior and remains intentionally unresolved without human confirmation; B must therefore stop at decisions with requirement-decision-pending, before Scenario Coverage, Binding or assignment. The required repository/requirements/decisions evidence stages and empty task and assignment expectations are consistent with that stop. The empty project team and capability claims do not create a prerequisite for reaching this earlier decision block and authorize no assignments. Supplied source evidence supports the listed owners: HTTPError formats the message, options types define the public and normalized contracts, Ky normalizes and exposes snapshots, and constants registers filtered Ky options. Merge, filtering, exports and hook/instance declarations are inspection owners, not mandatory edits where existing generic behavior suffices. Build configuration supports generated distribution declarations rather than separately maintained declaration owners; test-d is included in the explicit TypeScript check, distinct from AVA/tsx execution. Truncated existing test excerpts do not prevent judging this decision-stage expectation. Gold and preview release fingerprints agree, and supplied provenance explains the distinct original/saved PRD, manifest/evaluation source and source/bundled prompt digest domains. Historical project reuse does not establish capability scope or resolve DEC-001, and a fixed hypothetical C would not constitute a human Decision. This approval concerns the supplied pending case, not execution readiness or an independently reviewed paired-case bundle. I relied on Service-calculated, mechanically bound fingerprints; I did not recompute digests, execute code, inspect candidate outputs or provide human attestation.
